questions.stem: A pricing method runs `for (Item i : basket) { lock.lock(); total += price(i); }` and then a single `lock.unlock()` after the loop. A worker thread calls it for a basket of three items. Afterwards, a second thread calls `lock.lock()`. What happens?

options.text: The worker finishes; the second thread then waits indefinitely, since the worker's one unlock() gave back one of its three holds
options.says: the lock counts holds per thread: three lock() calls and one unlock() leave two holds, and the lock is free only at zero

options.text: The worker finishes; the second thread then gets the lock, since the worker's one unlock() gave back all three of its holds
options.says: unlock() takes away one hold; the lock is free only when the hold count is back to zero

options.text: The worker stops at its second lock(), since that call waits for the hold the worker already has
options.says: the lock is reentrant: the thread that holds it gets it again at once and the count goes up

options.text: The worker stops at its unlock(), since unlocking once after locking three times throws IllegalMonitorStateException
options.says: the owner may unlock while it still holds the lock; IllegalMonitorStateException comes from a thread that doesn't hold it

origin.section: The Lock Counts Holds: One unlock() per lock(), by the Thread That Holds It

questions.stem: An upload handler calls `lock.lock()` on the request thread, starts an asynchronous upload and returns. The upload's completion callback runs on a thread of the I/O pool and calls `lock.unlock()`. What happens when the first upload completes?

options.text: The callback's unlock() throws, and the lock stays held, since only the thread that took the lock may release it
options.says: the holds belong to the request thread; unlock() from any other thread throws IllegalMonitorStateException, and the lock stays held

options.text: The callback's unlock() returns normally, and the lock is free, since any thread may release it once the work is done
options.says: a ReentrantLock has an owner; releasing a permit from another thread is what a semaphore allows

options.text: The callback's unlock() throws, and the lock is already free, since the handler's return released it earlier
options.says: nothing releases a ReentrantLock but unlock(); returning from the handler doesn't, so the lock is still held

options.text: The callback's unlock() returns normally, and the lock is free, since the request thread's hold passed to the pool
options.says: the holds stay with the thread that took them, also when it goes back to its pool; they never move to another thread

origin.section: The Lock Counts Holds: One unlock() per lock(), by the Thread That Holds It

questions.stem: A dispatcher holds `lock` and calls a helper that locks the same lock again and then calls `ready.await()` on a condition created from that lock. While the dispatcher waits, a producer thread calls `lock.lock()`. What does the producer get?

options.text: It gets the lock at once, since await() lets go of both holds while the dispatcher waits
options.says: await() releases all of the thread's holds while it waits and gives them back before it returns

options.text: It gets the lock at once, since await() ends the dispatcher's ownership until it calls lock() again
options.says: await() takes the lock again by itself before it returns, with the same hold count as before

options.text: It waits until the dispatcher is signalled, since await() lets go of one hold and the other stays
options.says: await() releases all of the thread's holds, not just one

options.text: It waits until the dispatcher is signalled, since a thread waiting on a condition keeps the lock it holds
options.says: await() releases the lock while the thread waits; that is what lets another thread change the state

origin.section: A Condition Gives Up the Lock While It Waits, So Check Again After await()

questions.stem: A fair `ReentrantLock` guards a ledger, and five posting threads wait for it in `lock()`. A health check calls `lock.tryLock()` at the moment the lock is released. What happens to the health check's call?

options.text: It returns at once, and it can take the lock ahead of the five, since tryLock() ignores the queue
options.says: the javadoc and the run agree: tryLock() barges even on a fair lock; tryLock(0, SECONDS) respects the queue

options.text: It returns at once, and it can't take the lock ahead of the five, since a fair lock serves the longest waiter
options.says: that is what lock() and tryLock(0, SECONDS) see on a fair lock; the untimed tryLock() ignores the queue

options.text: It waits behind the five, since a fair lock serves requests in the order they arrived
options.says: tryLock() never waits; and on a fair lock it doesn't respect the queue either

options.text: It waits behind the five, since tryLock() on a fair lock queues the way lock() does
options.says: the untimed tryLock() returns at once, with or without the lock

origin.section: A Non-Fair Lock Lets a Newcomer Go First; a Fair Lock Queues, and Costs Throughput
